Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into  the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}-\int \frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}\cdot 4\,\text{d}x. \\  & =x{e}^{4x}-\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}4x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & ={x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/2}-{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/2}-{\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{4(1/2)}-0\cdot {e}^{4\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{4(1/2)}-{e}^{4\cdot 0}] \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}-0]-\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{2}-1] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({e}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
